items.summary: The Iran SNSC determination on the Hormuz re-closure remains unannounced through Sunday evening — Day 10 of contested compliance and the third full day since Majlis ratification confirmed the SNSC as the formal decision node. The weekend window — identified in Saturday's brief as the 'final pre-Monday frame' — expired without a formal announcement of any kind: no suspension of re-closure, no conditional retraction, no IRGC disciplinary framing, no public communication from the SNSC body. The re-closure is formally operative entering Monday June 29. The IRGC cargo ship strike (June 26, four one-way attack drones launched from Iranian-controlled territory, one impacting the upper deck of an IMO-backed cargo vessel on the Oman corridor route) advances to Day 3 without SNSC acknowledgment, attribution, or disciplinary framing of any kind. The IMO 118-tanker evacuation convoy framework remains paused following the strike. The extended SNSC silence through three post-ratification days and four post-strike days is the brief's most structurally opaque sustained development: the decision body is either paralyzed by factional division between IRGC-aligned hardliners and Pezeshkian pragmatist bloc, or is conducting deliberate strategic ambiguity to extract additional concessions from the Swiss technical framework (nuclear inspection access, asset repatriation timelines, phased sanctions-waiver extensions) before issuing a formal announcement. Both interpretations are structurally negative for the pump-relief chain. The 60-day oil sanctions waiver (through ~August 18) and Gulf producer output increases provide some supply-positive offset, but Lloyd's normalization — the upstream gate for the tanker-backlog-to-pump-relief chain — formally requires an SNSC position change that has not been issued. Iran's Foreign Minister has publicly stated 'no tangible progress' on key sticking points including uranium enrichment levels and Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile disposition. Switzerland Round 2 technical framework negotiations remain active but unresolved on the nuclear inspection and asset dispute parameters. Lebanon ceasefire advances to Hour ~148+ through Sunday without a formal void declaration — surpassing all durability thresholds. The Rubio framework (announced June 26: Hezbollah end hostilities and withdraw from southern Lebanon; Israel commits not to target Beirut's southern suburbs; pilot coordination zones established) is operative and represents the most significant diplomatic scaffolding since the MOU signing. However, Netanyahu's explicit and repeated refusal to set any withdrawal timeline from the southern Lebanon buffer zone ('we will stay as long as necessary'; IDF occupying approximately 570 km²) remains the primary structural constraint on SNSC domestic justification: the body cannot credibly frame a re-closure retraction as conditioned on Lebanese-front resolution while Israeli forces hold 570 km² of Lebanese territory without a phased withdrawal commitment. WTI closed Friday at $69.40 (Sunday markets closed) — Day 7 below the $74 normalization-confidence floor. The front-running gap between market sentiment and structural reality is now at its maximum width: sub-$70 WTI while 118 commercial tankers remain commercially stranded, Lloyd's war-risk premiums hold at 3-8% of vessel value versus 0.25% pre-conflict, and the IMO convoy framework is paused. Monday morning's opening is the first real market test of whether the supply-positive narrative holds without an SNSC announcement. Oregon pump prices approximately $5.35/gallon; national approximately $4.56/gallon; pump relief remains fully gated on the SNSC-to-Lloyd's-to-backlog-to-supply-pulse chain. Vice President Vance and Iranian state media continue to clash over IAEA inspector access to bombed Iranian nuclear sites — an ongoing friction point in the Swiss framework that the extended SNSC silence amplifies.

Kim's June 25 weapons tests — special-mission tactical ballistic missile warhead, upgraded multiple rocket launch systems, extended-range self-propelled gun-howitzer — were evaluated as demonstrating a 'deadly and destructive offensive posture' and represent the most concentrated North Korean capability demonstration since the brief cycle opened. Crimea fuel restrictions remain in emergency status following Ukrainian infrastructure strikes. G7 summit (France, June 15-17) pledged increased military assistance and expanded Russia sanctions. Ukrainian net territorial gains of approximately 100 square miles (April 28 to May 26) represent the highest rate of gain since the 2023 offensive; Zaporizhzhia and Kupyansk corridors active. items.summary: The East Cascades fire season onset arrived on schedule Sunday June 28 — the T-1 anticipated in Saturday's brief has advanced to Day 1 active. No catastrophic new ignitions were reported through Sunday evening, and the PNW enters the onset period with the strongest suppression resource baseline of the brief cycle. The Peterson Fire (Saturday June 27 afternoon, Alderdale/Klickitat County, WA, approximately 4,000 acres of grassland, northeast of Roosevelt) was the onset period's first significant ignition event — but was quickly contained. Evacuation 'Go Now' orders for residents between Alderdale Road and Peterson Road were issued by approximately 3 p.m. Saturday and fully lifted by 9 p.m. Saturday evening, with the fire contained by the time orders were rescinded. The Peterson Fire's same-day containment is a direct demonstration of the resource availability advantage secured by Kartar Fire's full containment (declared Saturday morning). Four large fires remain active in Washington state, but all are in late-containment or mop-up phases: Tule Road approximately 97%, Juniper Dunes approximately 93%, Upriver in final mop-up. Active smoke-generating fires in eastern Washington and Oregon include Garred Road and Lytle. Burn bans remain in effect across multiple Oregon and Washington counties. NSF Newport OR continues operational per the June 26 Trump administration reversal — the Endurance Array coastal atmospheric anchor for fire-weather modeling is intact entering the onset period. BPA grid stable Day 9 post-heat-advisory with no forced outages. NIFC PL3 Day 12. Oregon EO 26-10 Day 15: 414+ fires and approximately 8,000+ acres YTD. National 2026 context: approximately 2.6 million acres burned YTD nationally, nearly double the 2025 pace; above-average significant wildfire potential forecast for the entire PNW through September 2026, with comparisons drawn to the 2015 season (worst in regional history). Southwest Power Pool (SPP) West Balancing Authority Resource Advisory extended through Sunday June 27 citing seasonal heat load elevation, reduced wind and solar generation forecasts — a precautionary grid-reliability signal for the broader Western Interconnection that compounds the BPA hydroelectric stress context.

items.summary: CISA's CI Fortify initiative is the operative critical infrastructure posture framework, with the IRGC cargo ship strike (June 26, Day 3 unaddressed) representing the most significant deterioration of the implicit MOU constraint on IRGC cyber operations targeting US energy infrastructure. The 'post-MOU IRGC cyber window' is assessed as more open Sunday evening than at any point in the compliance period: three days without SNSC disciplinary framing of the strike, combined with the re-closure remaining formally operative, removes the deterrence signaling that the MOU diplomatic track had placed on IRGC offensive operations. CISA guidance requires critical infrastructure operators to develop offline operational capabilities for prolonged internet and telecom outages. NERC reports the US grid acquires approximately 60 new vulnerable points daily from digitalization acceleration, distributed energy resource integration, and third-party vendor dependencies. DOE 202(c) emergency power plant orders (Section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act) are producing significantly less energy than before their emergency designations, raising near-term reliability questions for the plants originally justified on emergency need grounds — a structural efficiency gap in the grid reliability backstop. NTIA's BEAD Restructuring Policy Notice for the $42.5 billion Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment program confirms most in-flight approved projects will not complete until 2027, with fiber supply chain constraints hitting smaller operators hardest. Air cargo freight rates remain elevated following the Hormuz crisis: rates have peaked but the decline is projected to be slow, with high rates and capacity constraints expected through Q3 2026 — a supply chain cost floor with direct implications for PNW logistics operators. FERC large-load show-cause orders advance to Day 12; AI data center pathway explanation deadline at T-18 (~July 18). The AI capex acceleration driving the FERC inquiry is the grid's most acute medium-term structural challenge — data center power demand curves are estimated to outpace transmission capacity buildout by 3-5 years. Water infrastructure authorization expires September 30, 2026; over 60% of US utilities operating beyond intended lifespan.

items.summary: East Cascades fire season onset has officially arrived — Sunday June 28 is Day 1 of the operational onset window anticipated throughout the June brief cycle. The news from Day 1 is operationally positive: no catastrophic new ignitions were reported through Sunday evening. The Peterson Fire (Klickitat County, approximately 4,000 acres of grassland, June 27 Saturday afternoon) demonstrated the resource advantage entering onset: ignition was rapid in dry grassland conditions northeast of Roosevelt; evacuation 'Go Now' orders for the Alderdale-Peterson Road corridor were issued around 3 p.m. Saturday and fully lifted by 9 p.m. Saturday, with containment achieved the same evening. The quick-containment result — made possible by the full aerial and ground resources freed by Kartar's 100% containment declaration earlier Saturday — is the strongest operational positive of the onset window opening. Four active Washington large fires remain in late-containment or mop-up phases: Tule Road approximately 97%, Juniper Dunes approximately 93%, Upriver in final mop-up. Active smoke-generating fires in eastern Washington and Oregon include Garred Road and Lytle. Burn bans in effect across multiple Oregon and Washington counties. NSF Newport OR continues operational — the Endurance Array coastal atmospheric anchor for fire-weather modeling is intact entering the onset period. BPA grid stable Day 9 post-heat-advisory. NIFC PL3 Day 12. Oregon EO 26-10 Day 15. The 2026 national wildfire season context remains sobering: approximately 2.6 million acres burned YTD nationally (nearly double the 2025 pace); above-average significant wildfire potential forecast for the entire PNW through September 2026. The comparison baseline — the 2015 worst-in-regional-history season — is the structural risk envelope for the summer ahead. The SPP West Balancing Authority Resource Advisory (June 27, extended) reflects seasonal heat load elevation across the broader Western grid that compounds the BPA hydroelectric generation stress from Columbia River flows at 54% of normal.

items.summary: Columbia River basin water crisis continues to deepen entering the East Cascades onset window. Columbia River streamflow at 340,000 cfs — approximately 54% of historical normal — reflects compounding effects of the record-low snowpack (winter 2025-26 tied 1934 as warmest on record at most mid-elevation stations), Drought Year 4, and the absence of meaningful precipitation recharge. At 54% of normal, BPA hydroelectric generation capacity is structurally compromised — creating an electricity cost premium that compounds Washington state's already elevated rate environment. Washington state electricity rates rose 13.2% year-over-year from 2025 (fifth-highest national increase) and the state has fallen from first to seventh in industrial electricity affordability over the past decade — a structural competitive disadvantage for Washington's data center and manufacturing base at the precise moment AI infrastructure investment is accelerating regionally. Washington drought emergency advances to Day 26 — fourth consecutive drought year, 12 emergency counties, 23 reservoir systems below historical averages. Oregon: 83% of state in drought; 17 counties under emergency order; Wasco and Malheur counties have additionally requested declarations. Super El Niño watch continues at 25% probability; base El Niño probability approximately 61% (KLCC/OPB June 22). A Super El Niño in 2026-2027 would produce a fifth consecutive critically dry, warm PNW winter — the single most consequential long-range regional risk factor. ENSO monitoring update expected early July. Technology sector: Bungie (Sony, Bellevue, WA) announced 292 employee layoffs as part of Sony restructuring — adding to the Amazon WARN (2,198 positions) as PNW tech-sector headcount contraction continues in parallel with AI infrastructure investment acceleration, deepening the structural bifurcation. FIFA World Cup PNW venues have driven record-breaking Sound Transit light rail ridership, with single-day boarding records broken twice in one week; matches continue through July 7. L-Pod orca calf continues alive entering Week 6 — a continued positive signal for the critically endangered Southern Resident Killer Whale population under sustained Chinook pressure. Oregon's 21st gray whale washup of 2026 (Lincoln City area) is the ongoing marine mammal stress indicator. Seattle-Tacoma area FIFA World Cup infrastructure (Port of Seattle SEA Concourse C expansion, light rail, stadium operation) continues through July 7.
